title: Inventory by warehouse
purpose: Cleans the SKU codes of the warehouse stock list, drops empty stock, and writes two views of it: one row per SKU and family with a quantity column per warehouse (INVENTORY_BY_WH), and the same quantities as one row per SKU and warehouse (INVENTORY_LONG).

outputs.grain: one row per SKU and family

columns.name: FAMILY
columns.meaning: The letters before the dash of the SKU; NULL when the SKU did not match

columns.name: EAST
columns.meaning: Total QTY in the EAST warehouse for the SKU and family; NULL when it has no stock rows there

columns.name: NORTH
columns.meaning: Total QTY in the NORTH warehouse for the SKU and family; NULL when it has no stock rows there

columns.name: WEST
columns.meaning: Total QTY in the WEST warehouse for the SKU and family; NULL when it has no stock rows there

outputs.grain: one row per pivot row and warehouse (EAST, NORTH, WEST), without the family

columns.name: NAME
columns.meaning: Warehouse the value comes from: EAST, NORTH or WEST

columns.name: VALUE
columns.meaning: Total quantity of the SKU in that warehouse; NULL when it has none

steps.name: Read warehouse stock
steps.does: Reads the STOCK list: SKU, WAREHOUSE, QTY and NOTE.

steps.name: Clean SKU codes and drop empty stock
steps.does: Runs the clean_codes macro with MinQty = 1: normalises each SKU to FAMILY-NUMBER form in upper case (a SKU that does not match is kept as it was) and drops the rows whose QTY is below 1 or NULL.

steps.name: Split SKU into family and item
steps.does: Parses SKU into FAMILY (the letters) and ITEM_NO (the digits); a SKU that does not match keeps its row with both NULL.

steps.name: Pivot quantity by warehouse
steps.does: Sums QTY per SKU and FAMILY with one column per warehouse (EAST, NORTH, WEST) and writes INVENTORY_BY_WH.

steps.name: Unpivot to one row per warehouse
steps.does: Turns the EAST, NORTH and WEST columns back into Name and Value rows per SKU and writes INVENTORY_LONG.

rules: The macro's question MinQty is 1, as the workflow passes it, not the macro's own default of 0: stock with QTY below 1 or NULL is dropped.
A SKU that is not letters, then a dash or space, then digits is kept unchanged by the macro and then has NULL FAMILY and ITEM_NO.
A SKU and warehouse with no stock rows is NULL in the pivot, never 0.
The warehouse columns are the three the pivot was built with (EAST, NORTH, WEST); stock for any other warehouse has no column and is left out.
INVENTORY_LONG has a row for every cell of the pivot, NULL cells included: three rows per pivot row.

parity_risks.note: The Input tool declares the four fields it expects (SKU 30, WAREHOUSE 10, QTY Int32, NOTE 100). The mapped Snowflake table has to present those names and families; the widths are the Alteryx widths and Snowflake does not enforce them when a table is created from a query.

A macro is a workflow, not a tool: there is no cookbook pattern for `macro`, only for the tools inside clean_codes.yxmc. Its inner tools are translated in place, and a change to the .yxmc file changes this translation even though inventory.yxmd did not change.
The question MinQty is 1 in the parent's <Value name="MinQty">, overriding the macro's own NumericUpDown default of 0. Translating the default instead would keep every zero-quantity row.

The macro's RegEx is Replace with CopyUnmatched, so a SKU that does not match is kept as it was rather than becoming NULL. REGEXP_REPLACE already returns the subject unchanged on no match, so the two agree -- but a translator who reached for a CASE with an ELSE NULL would not.

The macro's RegEx is case-INSENSITIVE (Alteryx spells the attribute CaseInsensitve), so `ab 12` and `zz9` normalise; the parent's RegEx at tool 3 is case-sensitive. The two flags are opposite and easy to swap.

The macro's Filter is [QTY] >= 1 and a NULL QTY makes that NULL, which is not true, so those rows leave on the unwired False anchor. That is what keeps a NULL WAREHOUSE (and a NULL SKU) out of the Cross Tab downstream, so SKU, WAREHOUSE and QTY are never NULL after the macro.

Snowflake's regex dialect is not Python's, which is what the simulator uses: \d and \s are ASCII-only in the local engine and Unicode-aware in the oracle, and case-insensitive [A-Za-z] folds differently at the edges of Unicode. No golden set contains a non-ASCII digit or a non-breaking space, so the divergence is recorded rather than guarded against.

RegEx Parse never drops a row: a SKU the pattern does not match keeps its row and leaves FAMILY and ITEM_NO NULL. On Snowflake REGEXP_SUBSTR returns NULL for that row; the local DuckDB double returns an empty string, so the match is tested with REGEXP_LIKE and the NULL written out explicitly.

This RegEx is case-SENSITIVE (^([A-Z]+)-(\d+)$), unlike the macro's. Every SKU reaching it has already been upper-cased inside the macro, so the flag changes nothing on this data -- but a non-ASCII initial (the edge set's ÄB-12) is outside [A-Z] under either flag, which is what leaves its FAMILY NULL.

A group/header combination with no rows is NULL, not zero. SUM over an empty set already gives NULL, so nothing may wrap the pivot in COALESCE -- and a row whose only value for a warehouse is NULL sums to NULL too.

The header columns are frozen by the tool's MetaInfo (EAST, NORTH, WEST) rather than discovered from the data, so the pivot is one conditional aggregate per column and a warehouse outside that list has no column and is dropped. Data with a fourth warehouse would silently lose it -- in Alteryx as well as here.
Cross Tab's Sum produces a Double whatever the data field's type, so the integer quantities land in a FLOAT column. The sum is taken over the exact NUMBER values and cast once.

Transpose keeps NULL values. A bare UNPIVOT drops a row whose value is NULL, but UNPIVOT INCLUDE NULLS keeps it too (see cookbook/transpose.md). The translation may instead stack three projections with UNION ALL, which also keeps every cell -- half the rows of this output.
The key field is SKU only, so FAMILY is dropped from the long table; the Name/Value pair is emitted per incoming row in the configured field order EAST, NORTH, WEST.
